title: 5DSTEM: Merging 4DSTEM and Core-Loss EELS: A Path to Detect Parameter-Free Electron Energy-Loss Magnetic Chiral Dichroism with Prospects of Atomic Resolution
content: Controlling and optimizing the electron orbital and spin degrees of freedom is crucial for the advancement of next generation spintronics and orbitronics devices [1, 2]. Currently only two techniques can map the spin and orbital angular momenta of electrons with element-specificity. X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) [3] is a widely used technique to map such magnetic moments, however its spatial resolution is limited to nanometer scales, and it requires access to a Synchrotron source which is not always readily available. Alternatively, such dichroic experiments can also be performed in a transmission electron microscope (TEM) or a scanning TEM (STEM) equipped with an electron energy loss (EELS) spectrometer, called electron energy loss chiral dichroism (EMCD) [4] in analogy with XMCD. Conducting EMCD experiments in a STEM offers the possibility of mapping orbital and spin moments of magnetic materials at atomic spatial resolution.
